source: Three files from one forum auctioneer (alesiev), converted from .xlsx to CSV without changing a value. They are the whole of Phase 5's spreadsheet-path evidence, and they disagree with each other about what a results file looks like.

knownDifferences: Patron Pin: the importer emits one row for a single-lot item, and the sheet carries two identical rows
files.why: The raw per-lot shape. `Number` is the lot number, not a quantity or a price — reading it as a price puts a $1 minimum on every item. This file also carries the 17 rows that belong in contextItems (9 Random UR, 6 Grunnel Augment, 2 Player Augment), so it is the abort case as well as the import case.

files.headers: Auction Item | Low Bid | High Bid
files.why: Already aggregated, so it contributes no rawPricesData rows — its two values per row are a min and a max, not two sales. It reconciles with 202640 and with nothing else (7 of 13 items on a min/max comparison against every 2026 auction; the runner-up scores 2), so the auction was MEASURED, not read off the filename, which says "#1" and is dated April. But it only agrees with the sheet on 6 of 13 items once the rows are built, and it differs in both directions — so this shape is imported with a caution, not trusted. Most of its names use the trailing-quantity spelling (AI 10x) and the abbreviations, so it is also the normalisation case. Golden Ticket | Withheld is the withheld marker.

files.headers: Row Labels | Minimum Bid | Maximum Bid | Average Bid
files.why: A pivot over EVERY bid received, not a record of winning bids. Read as winning bids it reconciles with none of that auctioneer's five auctions on a single item, and its ranges are far wider than the recorded prices — which is what a column of losing offers looks like. Nothing in the data says so; the `Average Bid` header is the only warning there is, which is why the importer refuses on the header.
